candidate: Jaguar Health, Inc. Series R Convertible Preferred Stock Dividend

new_primary_fact.source: Nasdaq Trader Equity Corporate Actions Alert #2026-731
facts: Nasdaq confirmed JAGX record date October 13, 2026 and payment date October 15, 2026.
Nasdaq described the special dividend as one Series R preferred share for each common share held.
Each Series R preferred share automatically converts into five common shares on November 2, 2026.
The alert initially listed the ex date as TBA, establishing that the exchange itself was managing the corporate-action clock.

issuer_update.fact: Jaguar later announced that Nasdaq set October 16, 2026 as the ex-dividend date and advised that common shares trade with due bills from the October 13 record date until the ex date; sellers during that period transfer the dividend right to buyers.

clock_resolution: The earlier blocker 'exact primary Nasdaq due-bill/ex-date route not preserved' is materially improved: Nasdaq Trader is now preserved as a primary exchange corporate-action source and the issuer's October 14 update states Nasdaq's October 16 ex-date/due-bill treatment. This validates the mechanism/clock class, not profitability.

current_case_contamination.reason: While locating the exchange clock, a third-party search result exposed a contemporaneous JAGX market-price snippet. Therefore this already-live October 2026 event cannot be promoted as a clean prospective economic observation under a protocol declared afterward. The price snippet is quarantined and must not be copied into research results or used to choose quantity, direction, entry, hedge, threshold or horizon.

remaining_gates: A future event must be declared before selected market-price exposure.
The distributed security/conversion terms must be reconstructible without outcome-dependent interpretation.
A lawful total-return route must value the common plus due-bill entitlement and later conversion shares, including dilution/corporate-action adjustments.
Beneficial-owner due-bill delivery and any restrictions on the distributed security must be publicly documentable.
A future protocol must forbid common-only pre/post-ex returns that omit the entitlement.
future_expression_boundary: The only scientifically admissible future question is whether a newly announced large non-cash due-bill distribution is mispriced as a PACKAGE (common + transferable dividend right + eventual conversion/delivery), after fixed costs and dilution accounting. Direction is not assumed. A common-price drop by itself is not edge and cannot be treated as loss/profit without the entitlement leg.
disconfirmation: Exchange due-bill mechanics are designed precisely to keep dividend entitlement attached to trades through the ex-date, reducing naive record-date arbitrage.
The preferred's automatic conversion into common shares makes the package economically linked to dilution rather than external cash value.
Broker processing and delivery delays can eliminate any theoretical package spread.
next_action: Do not run JAGX October 2026 economics. Preserve the Nasdaq Trader route as reusable mechanism evidence. If a future causally similar due-bill special-stock dividend appears, preregister event selection, package valuation, clock, quantity, costs and one adversary before any selected price payload. Otherwise keep the family documentary-only.
